data.title: SLB surges on strong Q3 results, upbeat 2027 outlook as Middle East rebounds
data.description:
SLB (SLB) surged 6.5% in Friday's trading after topping Q3 adjusted earnings and revenue estimates while signaling an upbeat 2027 as Middle East activity gradually recovers and Venezuela revenue is expected to more than double.

SLB (SLB) said it has seen a gradual recovery in its Middle East business—the company's biggest ‌market, ⁠accounting for 34% of total revenue in 2025 - despite disruptions from the Iran war, and Q3 revenue from the region rose 13% Q/Q.

The company expects Venezuela to be a "significant growth driver," with revenue on track to more than double by year-end and grow even more in 2027 as international operators ramp up investments, CEO Olivier Le Peuch said during ​the company's earnings conference call.

Overall, Q3 international revenue ticked up 1% to $6.99B, while North American revenue jumped 24% to $2.4B.

Le Peuch said AI demand is driving unprecedented investment in data center infrastructure, and SLB (SLB) is expanding its capabilities to capitalize on the demand, including through its planned $4.1B acquisition of thermal management company Kelvion and the recent buildout of a manufacturing center in Canada.

"We continue to strengthen our position as an industrial technology partner to the data-center industry and to expand our participation in this rapidly growing market," Le Peuch said on the earnings call.

Looking ahead, SLB (SLB) expects global oilfield services activity to grow by a mid-single-digit percentage in 2027, assuming Middle East activity remains at H2 2026 levels and that regional tensions do not escalate further.

data.title: Flagstar forecasts 2027 EPS of $0.85-$0.95 and shifts full turnaround timeline to 2028 amid higher rates
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Flagstar Bank (FLG) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "Net interest income increased, the net interest margin expanded and pre-provision net revenue improved compared to the previous quarter," while Flagstar "grew our C&I loan portfolio and deposits while reducing our exposure to commercial real estate loans this quarter" (CEO & Executive Chairman Joseph Otting).
  • "Given a higher for longer interest rate environment, the full realization of our transformation has shifted to 2028 from 2027," and "we are adjusting our guidance" to reflect "higher interest rates," "less deposit growth" and related impacts on "C&I loan growth" and "the net interest margin" (CEO & Executive Chairman Otting).
  • "This quarter, we delivered another $2 billion of net C&I loan growth"; CRE payoffs "totaled $1.2 billion"; and Flagstar had "net charge-offs of $74 million or 49 basis points of average loans" (CEO & Executive Chairman Otting).
  • "We've adjusted our guidance downward for both '26 and '27, predominantly the result of higher provision costs" tied to NYC rent-regulated multifamily sensitivity to "the forward curve with 4 rate hikes" and "inflationary pressures" (CFO, Co-President & Co-COO Lee Smith).
  • "We completed the previously approved stock repurchase program of $250 million" ("19.1 million shares" at "approximately $13 per share"), while "total deposits increased about $300 million quarter-over-quarter" and the "CET1 ratio" was "12.38%" (CFO, Co-President & Co-COO Smith).
  • "During the third quarter, we generated $4.6 billion in new and increased C&I loan commitments" and "C&I loans during the third quarter increased $2 billion to $20.6 billion"; Flagstar also had a "strong pipeline going into the fourth quarter at $2.7 billion" (Chief Banking Officer, Co-President & Co-COO Richard Raffetto).

Outlook

  • No usable analysts-estimates comparison was included because the provided estimates used an invalid fiscal-quarter format.
  • "EPS for '26 is now forecast to be in the $0.10 to $0.15 range and EPS for '27 is forecast to be in the $0.85 to $0.95 range"; Flagstar added a new view that "EPS is expected to be $1.60 to $1.70" in 2028 (CFO, Co-President & Co-COO Smith).
  • "We expect the balance sheet to grow on average approximately $1 billion a quarter in 2027 and 2028," driven by "net new loan growth of $2 billion" with funding split "approximately 50% with deposit growth and 50% with CRE runoff" (CFO, Co-President & Co-COO Smith).
  • Management framed 2027 as an inflection driven by contractual repricing: "between October 1, 2026, and December 31, '27, we have $12 billion of low coupon, less than 3.9% CRE multifamily loans either resetting or maturing" (CFO, Co-President & Co-COO Smith).

Financial Results

  • "Our NIM expanded 4 basis points in Q3 versus Q2 to 2.17%, with the September NIM coming in at 2.23%" (CFO, Co-President & Co-COO Smith).
  • "We generated plus $0.13 of earnings" pre-credit provision in Q3, which "included a $22 million or $0.04 tax benefit" from settling "a legacy tax audit from 2020" (CFO, Co-President & Co-COO Smith).
  • "We still expect full year '26 operating expenses to decline approximately $168 million or 9% year-over-year versus full year 2025" (CFO, Co-President & Co-COO Smith).
  • Credit metrics and reserves discussed on the call included: "an increase in our provision expense to $76 million in the third quarter"; "nonaccrual loans were relatively stable" at "approximately $2.8 billion"; and "criticized and classified loans increased $670 million or 6%" (CFO, Co-President & Co-COO Smith).

Q&A

  • Christopher McGratty, KBW: Asked about reset/maturity visibility; CFO Smith: "2027 is our biggest reset and maturity year" and migration was "very formulaic" using DSCR, with "the vast majority of the migration this quarter" on market units.
  • Christopher McGratty, KBW: Asked about buybacks given CET1 vs. target; CEO Otting: "don't envisage us doing any additional stock buybacks in the fourth quarter" and "would expect to resume buybacks in 2027."
  • David Rochester, Cantor Fitzgerald: Asked about deposit capture from C&I; CBO Raffetto: Flagstar brought "just under $600 million of deposits" on "$2 billion" net C&I growth, and "we feel pretty good about bringing in 30% of deposits."
  • David Rochester, Cantor Fitzgerald: Asked about confidence in 2028 ramp; CFO Smith: said the company added bridge slides because key drivers are "balance sheet growth" and "fixed asset repricing," while deposit assumptions were detailed, including new deposit cost assumptions of "between 3.9% and 4%."
  • David Chiaverini, Jefferies: Asked what is most at risk in NII drivers; CFO Smith: deposit growth is the key question—"can we deliver on the deposit growth"—while repricing is "all mechanical."
  • Casey Haire: Asked about net charge-offs guide and deposit beta; CFO Smith: "I would look at that as the proxy for net charge-offs" (provision forecast), and deposit beta targeting included "we are targeting a 60% beta."
  • Jared Shaw, Barclays: Asked about growth assumptions and rent-reg landlord sentiment; CFO Smith: growth is "predicated on the deposit" and "90% of the growth is going to come from C&I"; CEO Otting: borrowers may want "the bank to restructure and lower their interest rate off the contractual coupon."
  • David Smith, Truist: Asked for ending assets; CFO Smith: "end of '26... $82.1 billion" and "end of '27, $92.1 billion... end of '28... around $97 billion."
  • Ryan Kenny, Morgan Stanley: Asked about noninterest-bearing deposit growth; CFO Smith: the shift reflected reclassifying "$900 million to $1 billion" of very low-rate interest-bearing accounts to noninterest-bearing.
  • Ebrahim Poonawala, BofA: Pressed on suspending buybacks; CEO Otting: "it's prudent until we build our core earnings and ensure that our credit quality forecast is accurate"; on M&A, CEO Otting: "we think the best value... is for us to execute on our business plan."
  • Benjamin Gerlinger, Citigroup: Asked curve timing and rate sensitivity; CFO Smith: forecast used "a September curve that had 4 hikes" and added, "If rates come down, that is definitely beneficial" for credit.
  • Anthony Elian, JPMorgan: Asked about selling rent-regulated exposure; CEO Otting: "we have currently like nothing on the table to do that" and said internal resolutions have been "with 1% to 5%" near marks while investors target "15% to 20% returns."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone skewed slightly negative and pressing around buybacks, rate sensitivity, and rent-regulated exposure, including "why are we shutting down the buybacks?" and whether the franchise is "very much an interest rate curve bet" (Ebrahim Poonawala, BofA Securities; Benjamin Gerlinger, Citigroup).
  • Management tone in prepared remarks was slightly positive on execution but tempered on timing, with CEO Otting saying the 2028 shift was "a change in timing, not in our strategy nor expectations," while Q&A included caution such as "it's prudent" to pause buybacks until credit and earnings visibility improve (CEO & Executive Chairman Otting).
  • Versus the prior quarter’s prepared confidence ("we are confident that we are on the right path"), the current call used more timing-and-macro framing ("higher for longer") and explicitly extended the turnaround timeline (CEO & Executive Chairman Otting).

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • In Q2, Flagstar announced "a $250 million share buyback" (CEO & Executive Chairman Otting); in Q3, management said it "completed" that program but "don't envisage" additional buybacks in Q4, with an expectation to "resume" in 2027 (CEO & Executive Chairman Otting).
  • Guidance language shifted materially: Q2 said "EPS for '26... $0.40 to $0.50" and "EPS for '27... $1.60 to $1.70" (CFO, Co-President & Co-COO Smith); Q3 reset to "$0.10 to $0.15" for 2026 and "$0.85 to $0.95" for 2027, while adding 2028 EPS guidance (CFO, Co-President & Co-COO Smith).
  • Strategy emphasis remained centered on C&I growth and CRE reduction, but Q3 added explicit timing slippage: "full realization of our transformation has shifted to 2028 from 2027" (CEO & Executive Chairman Otting).
  • Analyst focus broadened from Q2’s buyback authorization and NIM trajectory to Q3’s higher-rate credit implications, deposit competitiveness, and whether portfolio sales or strategic combinations were being considered.

Risks and Concerns

  • Management tied higher credit costs to "higher interest rates," "actions related to the New York City rent regulations" and "persistent inflationary pressures," while also citing "a competitive deposit environment" as a constraint (CEO & Executive Chairman Otting).
  • CFO Smith described a rate/inflation transmission into rent-regulated multifamily via "increased cap rates," "put pressure on debt service coverage ratios," and "increased the risk that more loans migrate to criticized and classified status," and linked this to higher provisioning.
  • On mitigation, management emphasized mechanical repricing and remixing: resets/maturities are "all contractual," and the plan relies on "reduce our New York rent-regulated exposure" and fund C&I growth with deposits plus CRE runoff (CEO & Executive Chairman Otting; CFO, Co-President & Co-COO Smith).

Final Takeaway

Management presented Q3 as continued operational progress—C&I growth, CRE runoff, and modest NIM improvement—but reset the investment narrative around a “higher for longer” rate backdrop that raised provision expense, tightened deposit-growth assumptions, and pushed “peer-like metrics” timing out by roughly a year. The updated earnings path centered on contractual CRE repricing and planned balance-sheet growth funded half by deposits and half by CRE runoff, while capital return shifted from completing the prior $250M program to pausing further buybacks in Q4 and pointing to a 2027 resumption tied to core earnings and credit visibility.

data.title: SA Asks: Why did the market sell off after relatively good earnings reports?
data.description:
Why did the market sell off this week after the release of relatively good earnings reports?

Seeking Alpha analysts Jack Bowman and Gytis Zizys offer their views.

Jack Bowman: With the recent drama surrounding CoreWeave (CRWV), the bell seems to be tolling for return on invested capital metrics. Top and bottom line beats, like with Tesla (TSLA), aren't meaningful if the market is suspecting that you're using that to plow straight into more capex without seeing the return. 

I don't know if this trend will hold. I think that hyperscaler earnings, especially those of Microsoft (MSFT) and Alphabet (GOOGL) (GOOG), which both report on Oct. 28, will determine market sentiment from here. If they're good, not just in the top and bottom lines, but also in cloud revenue growth, then I'd assume the bulls will come back. Miss those figures, and it may be rough sailing until mid-November, when Nvidia (NVDA) earnings come out.

Gytis Zizys: I think the main reason we are seeing such brutal price action, specifically in the Nasdaq (QQQ) and the S&P500 (SPY) to an extent, is because investors fear the AI growth narrative has seemingly run its course. Multiple companies reported increased demand across the board when it comes to AI growth; Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) and Micron (MU) have reported stellar earnings, but the sentiment is that it’s time to put the brakes on. 

The constant news around the U.S. and Iran flip-flopping isn’t helping the narrative, either. 

I don’t think the growth is over. At least that’s not what the fundamental picture of many companies that reported is saying. Meta Platforms (META) just reported great earnings, and capex spending will just increase next year. Other hyperscalers will follow suit.

It is also important to note that the picture looks worse than it is because the correction has mainly hit tech stocks, while most other sectors are faring much better. There’s too much concentration in AI names these days that is distorting the picture.

data.title: White House seen endorsing "U.S. Caught Seafood" labels - report
data.description:
The White House is expected to endorse a “U.S. Caught Seafood” label proposed by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to help consumers distinguish domestically caught seafood from imports, which account for more than three-quarters of U.S. seafood consumption. 

According to CBS citing government officials, President Trump is poised to support the new, non-mandatory labeling at a campaign stop in Fort Myers, Florida, on Friday. The Sunshine State is ranked ninth in the aquaculture industry with $72B in products sold.

The “U.S. Caught Seafood” label would also come with $5B in loans from the USDA to the domestic fishing industry for new equipment.

While the labeling is unlikely to have a meaningful impact on seafood sales in the U.S., grocers with a well-regarded seafood department include Sprouts Farmers Market (SFM), Amazon’s Whole Foods (AMZN), Albertsons Companies (ACI), Wegman’s, Market Basket, Meijer, and Kroger (KR).

Related tickers: Mowi Asa (MHGVY) (MNHVF), Lerøy Seafood Group (LYSFF) (LYSFY), Atlantic Sapphire (AASZF), SalMar (SALRF) (SALRY). Sysco Corp (SYY), US Foods Holding Corp (USFD), Performance Food Group (PFGC), The Chef’s Warehouse (CHEF).

Odds of oil reaching $110 by October-end rise to 34%
data.description:
Odds that WTI Crude Oil (CL1:COM) will rise above $110 per barrel by the end of the month have risen to 34%, according to predictions platform Polymarket.

 

 

Crude oil (CL1:COM) has risen more than 18% in the past three months and about 4% in the past week to be around $103 on Friday.

In addition, Brent Crude (CO1:COM) oil prices are now less than 2% away from their four-year high, at around $116 on Friday, up 18.3% in the past month alone.

Oil prices rose after reports that the U.S. and Israel could be drawing plans for attacks on Iran.

U.S. President Donald Trump also accused Iran of “doing everything they can to drive up the price of oil” prior to the midterm election.

“$100+ oil is back,” analysts at The Kobeissi Letter said.

data.title: First Bank targets $300m annual loan growth for 2027 as it launches $24m buyback
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: First Bank (FRBA) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "In the third quarter, we saw continued improvement." (President, CEO & Director Patrick Ryan) "Our balance sheet growth continued at a healthy pace, including loans, which were up $50 million during the quarter, and deposits, which increased $43 million during the quarter." (President, CEO & Director Ryan) "Our margin improved nicely to 3.74%, driving our return on average assets back up to 1.18%." (President, CEO & Director Ryan)

  • "Our strong capital position gives us significant flexibility" and "we intend to pull several levers to optimize our results moving forward." (President, CEO & Director Ryan) "We started by announcing an increase to our quarterly dividend, moving it up to $0.12 per share, a 33% increase." (President, CEO & Director Ryan) "We also announced our new buyback plan" and "see opportunities to leverage our capital for increased organic growth" as "our middle market commercial lending businesses gain momentum." (President, CEO & Director Ryan)

  • "For the 3 months ended September 30, 2026, we recorded net income of $12.2 million or $0.49 per diluted share." (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Andrew Hibshman) "Net interest income increased $2 million or 5.6% compared to the linked quarter." (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman) "Loan yields increased 15 basis points linked quarter to 6.48%, while our total cost of deposits increased only 5 basis points to 2.47% -- as a result, our tax equivalent net interest margin expanded 6 basis points to 3.74%." (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman)

  • "We successfully put that strategy into action this quarter by using excess liquidity to pay down $90 million in wholesale borrowings." (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman) "We've reduced brokered deposits by $44 million and purchased approximately $57 million of low-risk investment securities, offering higher yields than cash." (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman)

  • "New loans closed and funded during the quarter totaled $124 million" and "at September 30, probable funding stood at $363 million." (Executive VP & Chief Lending Officer Peter Cahill) "As a result of what we're seeing throughout the business units, as we think about 2027, we're setting our sights on total loan growth that's up from the $200 million annual number that we've targeted the past couple of years to a targeted growth rate closer to $300 million." (Executive VP & Chief Lending Officer Cahill)

Outlook

  • "I'm really expecting to see a stable margin. Hopefully, we can see some slight improvement in the margin going forward." (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman) "We should be able to maintain a stable margin with some upside." (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman)

  • "The competitive environment for deposits remains challenging." (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman) "We expect this will have an impact on our cost of interest-bearing deposits and put pressure on our noninterest-bearing balances." (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman)

  • Compared with Q2’s framing that the bank was "targeting flat to down slightly on the margin as we move through this year" (President, CEO & Director Ryan, prior quarter), Q3 messaging added rate-upside language: "we are slightly asset sensitive" and "if rates go higher, we do better." (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman)

Financial Results

  • "Loans grew $50.2 million or approximately 6% annualized" and deposit growth was "total deposits increasing $43 million or approximately 5% annualized." (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman) "Our high-yielding C&I portfolio grew to comprise 22.5% of total loans" at quarter-end. (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman)

  • "Provision expense was $2.2 million" and "we did see slightly higher net charge-offs of $1.9 million" that "primarily reflect activity in our Business Express portfolio." (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman) "This portfolio continues to run down, and we expect any future losses will moderate from recent quarters." (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman)

  • "Nonperforming assets rose slightly to $35.7 million" and "our allowance for credit losses remains essentially stable at 1.37% of total loans" and "represented approximately 132% of nonperforming loans." (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman)

  • "Noninterest expense was $20.3 million" and "our efficiency ratio improved to 52.4% from 54.5%" and marked "our 29th consecutive quarter operating below 60%." (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman)

  • "We also received final regulatory approval for a new share repurchase program, authorizing the repurchase of up to 1.2 million shares with an aggregate value of up to $24 million, which will run through September 2027." (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman)

Q&A

  • Bader Hijleh, Piper Sandler & Co.: "how you're thinking about maybe deposits continuing to keep pace to fund loan growth" and "the level of competition"; President, CEO & Director Ryan: "we continue to grow in our C&I book" and "we still play in the retail space" and "from time to time as needed, we'll get competitive with a market rate on a CD or money market." Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman: "deposit pricing pressure has continued to be stiff" and "I do expect that deposit pricing is going to be tough and it's going to move higher, but we think we can offset that in the loan book."

  • Bader Hijleh, Piper Sandler & Co.: asked to "quantify" asset repricing benefit; President, CEO & Director Ryan: "we've got 25% plus of our assets that reprice immediately when the Fed moves" and "we have a much smaller percentage of our liabilities that will reprice automatically." Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman: "day 1, when the Fed makes a rate change, we see positives" and "we should be able to maintain a stable margin with some upside."

  • Parker Wittmann, D.A. Davidson & Co.: asked about remaining Business Express exposure and when impacts become "less meaningful"; President, CEO & Director Ryan: "we're seeing a slowdown in new issues emerging" and "we feel comfortable saying that things are getting better" and "if we can get it back down to a more reasonable sort of 2%, even 3% annualized, I think we'll be back to generating profitability out of that segment."

  • David Bishop, Hovde Group: asked about improving the operating expense to average assets ratio toward "190"; President, CEO & Director Ryan: "the goal throughout '27 is to get to the 190" and "getting to that 190 at some point sort of during the middle of '27 is possible" and "longer term, could we get back to the 180? It's certainly possible."

  • David Bishop, Hovde Group: asked about loan origination yields; President, CEO & Director Ryan: "the market now for most new business is in the high 6s or 7s" and Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman: "the weighted average spread for the quarter was about 6.90%."

  • David Bishop, Hovde Group: asked whether higher rates are slowing CRE; President, CEO & Director Ryan: "we have not seen a significant pullback or slowdown" but "if they move again, is that a potential risk? Yes, certainly, it is."

  • David Bishop, Hovde Group: asked about the new leader; President, CEO & Director Ryan: "Dan Cuneo joined the team" and "Dan's got a breadth of experience at community banks and regional banks" in "Southern Jersey, Southeastern PA market."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analyst tone was neutral-to-slightly cautious, with repeated probing on deposits and pricing pressure ("level of competition"; "pricing pressure"), and targeted credit questions on Business Express runoff and CRE sensitivity to higher rates.

  • Management tone was slightly positive in prepared remarks ("continued improvement"; "prospects for even better profitability in 2027 look good") and measured in Q&A on deposit pricing and credit, using qualifying language such as "it's hard to predict" and "we'll see how the deposit market shapes up." (President, CEO & Director Ryan; Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman)

  • Versus Q2, Q3 added more confidence-linked capital actions (dividend increase and a newly approved buyback) and more explicit rate-sensitivity framing ("if rates go higher, we do better"), while acknowledging deposit pricing pressure as "accelerated" in the most recent month. (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q3 emphasized capital deployment levers: "increase to our quarterly dividend" and "new share repurchase program" with authorization "up to $24 million" through "September 2027"; Q2 discussed repurchases executed under the then-current program and described plans as "a stable cash dividend, and share buybacks as applicable over time." (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman; prior quarter)

  • Credit discussion shifted from Q2’s "signs of improvement" in the small business portfolio to Q3’s acknowledgement that Business Express still drove charge-offs, while stressing improvement signals ("slowdown in new issues"; "slightly lower delinquencies" in October). (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman; President, CEO & Director Ryan)

  • Loan-growth narrative moved from Q2’s focus on meeting the "$200 million loan growth goal" to Q3’s 2027 ambition "closer to $300 million." (President, CEO & Director Ryan; Executive VP & Chief Lending Officer Cahill)

Risks and Concerns

  • "The competitive environment for deposits remains challenging" and management expected pressure on "our cost of interest-bearing deposits" and "noninterest-bearing balances," with mitigation centered on "pricing discipline" and mix optimization, including paying down "$90 million in wholesale borrowings" and reducing brokered deposits by "$44 million." (Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman)

  • Business Express remained the primary credit issue: charge-offs "primarily reflect activity" there, with mitigation described as tighter standards ("much tighter standards" on originations and renewals) and an expectation that losses "will moderate." (President, CEO & Director Ryan; Executive VP, Treasurer & CFO Hibshman)

  • CRE sensitivity to rates was flagged as a contingent risk: "new projects... people might sharpen their pencil" and "if they move again" it is "a potential risk." (President, CEO & Director Ryan)

Final Takeaway

Management described Q3 as a step-up in profitability and efficiency alongside balance sheet growth, and tied that momentum to new capital actions—raising the quarterly dividend to $0.12 and launching a new repurchase authorization up to $24 million through September 2027—while positioning 2027 for higher organic growth, including a stated target to lift annual loan growth toward $300 million. At the same time, leadership repeatedly pointed to deposit pricing pressure and residual Business Express credit costs as the key near-term constraints, outlining balance-sheet optimization and tightening underwriting standards as the primary mitigants.

data.title: Moneyfarm rejects eToro's takeover offer - report
data.description:
Trading platform eToro Group's (ETOR) takeover offer for Moneyfarm was rejected by the European digital wealth manager, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg News.

The Israel-based company had offered to buy Moneyfarm for about €250M-€300M, according to the sources, who asked not to be named while discussing private information.

Moneyfarm considered the valuation too low, the sources reportedly noted.

The digital wealth manager's investors include M&G (MGPUF) (MGPFY), Allianz (ALIZF) (ALIZY), Poste Italiane (PITAF), United Ventures, and Cabot Square Capital.

data.title: Baidu and Lyft push ahead with plans for a robotaxi service in London
data.description:
Baidu (BIDU) showed off the company's RT6 autonomous vehicle in London this week as it moves toward launching a driverless robotaxi service in the city in 2027 in partnership with Lyft (LYFT).

Notably, Baidu's (BIDU) robotaxi unit has been testing its sixth-generation RT6 vehicles in London since July in partnership with Freenow by Lyft. The cars started out in the borough of Brent in northwest London, which has a mix of urban and suburban streets, and every test car carries a human safety operator, according to Lyft. Uber said the same day that Apollo Go vehicles were also running on London's public roads under its own separate deal with Baidu. Baidu called this the first time a Chinese self-driving car had been tested in London's traffic. It also followed Baidu's earlier launch in Hong Kong, which, like the UK, drives on the left.

The robotaxis are not meant to replace London's black cabs. Instead, Freenow by Lyft (LYFT) plans a mixed network where robotaxis run alongside its taxis and private-hire drivers.

Baidu (BIDU) is the third robotaxi company in London, after Waymo (WAYMO) and the Uber (UBER)–Wayve partnership.

data.title: Hilltop anticipates 7% to 8% full-year average loan growth in 2026 as deposit costs trend higher
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Hilltop Holdings (HTH) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "For the third quarter, Hilltop reported net income of $24.9 million or $0.44 per diluted share" (President, CEO & Chairman Jeremy Ford). "PlainsCapital Bank further realized growth in core loans and deposits while expanding net interest margin to deliver $44 million in pretax income" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford). "PrimeLending reported a pretax loss of $11 million as the mortgage market worked through a drastic intra-quarter increase in mortgage rates" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford). "HilltopSecurities delivered $7 million of pretax income as material interest rate volatility in the quarter pressured the trading business lines at the firm" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford).

  • "Net interest margin also expanded, increasing over 25 basis points on a year-over-year basis to 3.49%, driven by stable deposit costs and upward repricing of our loan portfolio" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford). "We expect there to be upward pressure on deposit costs going forward" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford).

  • "During the quarter, PlainsCapital Bank saw an increase in deposit balances of $500 million" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford). "In the fourth quarter, we anticipate deposit balance to continue to seasonally expand" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford). "Notably, PlainsCapital Bank increased deposits swept over from HilltopSecurities during the third quarter by $100 million" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford).

  • "In total, the mark-to-market losses capturing both rate and volume impacts that are reflected in the third quarter equated to approximately $16 million on a pretax basis" (Executive VP & CFO William Furr). "Hilltop's reported negative AOCI impact equated to approximately $21 million" (Executive VP & CFO Furr). "The quarter also included net valuation gains of $4.6 million related to Hilltop's merchant banking portfolio investments" (Executive VP & CFO Furr).

  • "Hilltop maintains strong capital levels with a common equity Tier 1 capital ratio of 18.3%" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford). "Our tangible book value per share realized a modest quarter-over-quarter decline to $32.20" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford). "During the quarter, we returned $33 million to stockholders, consisting of $12.6 million in dividends and $20 million in share repurchases" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford).

Outlook

  • "Our current internal rate outlook anticipates one additional 25 basis point rate increase in 2026" (Executive VP & CFO Furr). "Under this rate scenario, we expect that NII levels will continue to move modestly higher, largely driven by expected loan growth within our Banking segment" (Executive VP & CFO Furr).

  • "We do expect that interest-bearing deposit yields have reached their trough levels for the cycle and will likely trend higher with short-term market interest rates over time" (Executive VP & CFO Furr). "We would expect to see NIM level out and potentially travel a little lower from these levels from the 3.33% level" (Executive VP & CFO Furr).

  • Compared with the prior quarter’s rate scenario of "one rate increase to occur in December of 2026" (Executive VP & CFO Furr, Q2), management in Q3 said the market "decidedly" shifted toward "higher short-term interest rates" (Executive VP & CFO Furr) and reiterated an expectation for "upward pressure on deposit costs" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford).

Financial Results

  • "Net interest income in the third quarter equated to $122 million" (Executive VP & CFO Furr). "During the third quarter, net interest margin increased versus the second quarter of 2026 by 12 basis points to 333 basis points" (Executive VP & CFO Furr).

  • "Total noninterest income for the third quarter of 2026 equated to $187 million" (Executive VP & CFO Furr). "Mortgage revenues declined by $9 million" (Executive VP & CFO Furr), and "lock volume" in the quarter "declined 18% to $2.2 billion" (Executive VP & CFO Furr). "Gain on sale margins for loans sold to third parties declined 26 basis points to 200 basis points" (Executive VP & CFO Furr).

  • "Noninterest expenses declined from the same period in the prior year by $7.8 million to $264 million" (Executive VP & CFO Furr). "Looking forward, we expect that expenses other than variable compensation will remain relatively stable at current levels" (Executive VP & CFO Furr).

  • "Hilltop's allowance for credit losses increased during the quarter by $9 million to $94 million" (Executive VP & CFO Furr), and "NPA levels have declined from the second quarter of 2026 by $2 million to $60 million" (Executive VP & CFO Furr). "Net charge-offs for the quarter equated to $1.2 million or 6 basis points of the overall loan portfolio" (Executive VP & CFO Furr).

Q&A

  • Hannah Wynn, KBW: "Just curious how we should think about the puts and takes" in mortgage and whether to expect "continued losses" or expense reductions; Executive VP & CFO Furr: "we remain focused on productivity and adjusting the business to the current market environment" and "we're going to do everything in our power to drive toward profitability, but also support our LOs across the country".

  • Hannah Wynn, KBW: "Can you just talk about how much runway you still see" on NIM as deposit competition rises; Executive VP & CFO Furr: "we do continue to feel comfortable and confident in kind of the trajectory of NII" and "we would expect to see NIM level out and potentially travel a little lower".

  • Evan Yee, Raymond James: asked what drove the improved nonvariable expense outlook and next-year framing; Executive VP & CFO Furr: "we're very pleased we've been able to keep our expenses other than variable compensation stable" and "we believe expenses will be a little lower".

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were slightly negative, centering questions on mortgage profitability and how long pressure persists, including Wynn’s focus on "continued losses" and Yee’s probing on 2027 deposit growth.

  • Management tone was neutral to slightly positive on banking momentum, while more cautious on rate-driven volatility: Furr said "we do not anticipate any significant systemic risk across the portfolio" and Ford emphasized repurchase "prudence" given AOCI sensitivity.

  • Versus the prior quarter, management language shifted from a "muted start" in mortgage (President, CEO & Chairman Ford, Q2) to a sharper rate shock narrative in Q3, with Furr describing "substantial valuation adjustments" and Ford highlighting "drastic" rate increases.

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Profitability declined quarter over quarter as management reported Q3 net income of $24.9 million vs. Q2 net income of $36.5 million (President, CEO & Chairman Ford).

  • PrimeLending deterioration was a central change, moving from a Q2 pretax loss of $2 million to a Q3 pretax loss of $10.8 million (President, CEO & Chairman Ford), which management tied to September’s rapid rate move and hedge ineffectiveness.

  • Banking commentary remained constructive in both quarters on pipeline/recruiting, while Q3 added more explicit deposit-cost pressure: Q2 noted deposit costs were declining and NIM "will moderate" (Executive VP & CFO Furr, Q2), while Q3 said deposit yields hit a "trough" and will "trend higher" (Executive VP & CFO Furr).

Risks and Concerns

  • "There continues to be volatility in the interest rate markets" (Executive VP & CFO Furr) was framed as a primary driver of valuation marks in mortgage and broker-dealer trading, with Furr noting "hedge ineffectiveness" during the quarter.

  • Credit risk monitoring was reiterated amid macro uncertainty: "ongoing conflict in the Middle East, midterm elections and other issues that could contribute to credit risk" (Executive VP & CFO Furr), alongside the mitigation approach of monitoring for "early detection and aggressive workout when necessary" (Executive VP & CFO Furr).

  • Mortgage affordability constraints were described as persistent: "homeowners insurance, property taxes and entry-priced inventory, continue to stress volumes" (President, CEO & Chairman Ford), and Furr added, "we believe that these issues will negatively impact mortgage sales activity into 2027".

Final Takeaway

Management positioned Q3 as a quarter where PlainsCapital Bank’s loan/deposit growth and higher net interest income were offset by interest-rate volatility that drove mortgage and broker-dealer valuation losses and a larger credit provision. Into year-end, management emphasized an outlook for modestly higher net interest income on loan growth, while expecting deposit costs to rise and NIM to level out and potentially move lower, alongside continued efforts to rightsize PrimeLending and sustain capital returns within market and AOCI constraints.
